title: CuTe CUTLASS Float32 constructor accepts loc and ip keywords
applies_when: A CuTe DSL lead claims Float32(value, loc=loc, ip=ip) necessarily raises TypeError because another call attaches those keywords to ir_value instead.
lesson: Check the pinned dependency's Float constructor and Float32 inheritance before changing the call. The referenced CUTLASS implementation accepts keyword-only loc and ip; different valid spellings elsewhere do not establish an invalid constructor. A cheap installed-native signature bind and construction with a Python float and None metadata can discriminate the unsupported-keyword hypothesis without allocating a GPU or compiling a kernel. Confirm the dependency version and a live caller before proposing a repair.
avoid_when: This establishes accepted keyword names, not equivalence of metadata propagation or emitted IR. None metadata and a Python float do not exercise an actual MLIR Value, inline assembly, SASS, synchronization or kernel numerics. An older installed DSL does not qualify a newer FlashAttention dependency closure; verify exact versions when behavior matters. Reopen on a real constructor/IR failure in a supported caller, not merely a stylistic difference.

evidence.note: Pinned Float.__init__ declares keyword-only loc and ip; Float32 inherits Float. This is an API-source counterexample, not a kernel execution result.
e2e_asm2 uses Float32 with loc/ip constructor keywords. The presence of another ir_value spelling does not establish this call is invalid.
